q: Which description of cellular senescence is supported by Hazzard?
o: Nondividing cells persisting with secretion of inflammatory cytokines
Acceleration of cell division with suppression of inflammatory cytokines
Death and removal of cells following progressive telomere shortening
Resumption of cell division following activation of telomerase
explanation:
Cellular senescence is a lasting arrest of cell division. A senescent cell remains metabolically active and can change the environment around it.

**Senescent cells can persist and release inflammatory cytokines. This explains how cells that have stopped multiplying can still affect nearby tissue.**

**A. Persistent, nondividing cells that secrete cytokines.** A senescent fibroblast can remain alive after growth stops and release cytokines that act on neighboring cells.
**B. Faster division with suppressed cytokine release.** Growth arrest is central to senescence, and inflammatory secretion can continue after the cell stops dividing.
**C. Death after telomere shortening.** Critically short telomeres can trigger either cell death or senescence. The senescent cell survives the arrest, whereas a dead cell is eventually cleared.
**D. Renewed division after telomerase activation.** Telomerase helps maintain chromosome ends. Renewed proliferation would indicate that the cell is dividing again, which conflicts with persistent growth arrest.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 13.
ref: Hazzard Ch 1 — BIOLOGY OF AGING AND LONGEVITY

q: בבירור חשד לפגיעה בקשיש נמצא שאדם אחר משתמש ברכושו ללא רשותו. כיצד מסווגת פגיעה זו בחוזר משרד הבריאות 22/03?
o: התעמרות כלכלית עקב שימוש ברכוש ללא רשות
התעמרות פיזית עקב פגיעה ישירה בגוף האדם
הזנחה עקב כשל במילוי צורכי המחיה הבסיסיים
התעמרות נפשית עקב פגיעה ברווחה הרגשית
explanation:
לקיחת כסף או שימוש ברכוש בלי רשות הם ניצול כלכלי גם כאשר עושה זאת אדם המטפל בזקן. **התעמרות כלכלית עקב שימוש ברכוש ללא רשות**.

**א. התעמרות כלכלית עקב שימוש ברכוש ללא רשות.** השימוש הבלתי מורשה הוא הפגיעה המתוארת.
**ב. התעמרות פיזית עקב פגיעה ישירה בגוף האדם.** לא תוארה הפעלת כוח על גופו.
**ג. הזנחה עקב כשל במילוי צורכי המחיה הבסיסיים.** לא תואר חסך בהזנה, בהיגיינה או בטיפול.
**ד. התעמרות נפשית עקב פגיעה ברווחה הרגשית.** פגיעה רגשית עשויה להתלוות למעשה אך אינה מאפיינו העיקרי.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 4.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

q: A 78-year-old man screens positive on SARC-F and reports difficulty rising from a chair, climbing stairs, and a recent fall. In the EWGSOP2 approach described by Hazzard, which measurement comes next?
o: Estimate muscle mass using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
Assess physical performance using a standardized gait-speed test
Measure handgrip strength using a validated dynamometer protocol
Measure serum vitamin D and testosterone concentrations
explanation:
EWGSOP2 moves from case finding to strength assessment, then to confirmation and severity assessment. **The immediate next test is grip strength using a validated dynamometer protocol.**

**A. DXA lean mass** Estimating appendicular lean mass helps confirm the muscular basis of weakness after low strength is documented.
**B. Gait speed** Gait speed measures whole-body performance and helps grade severity once sarcopenia is confirmed.
**C. Standardized handgrip** Measure the force the patient can generate and compare it with the appropriate reference values. The questionnaire alone has not measured strength.
**D. Vitamin D and testosterone** Targeted blood tests may contribute to a search for underlying illness. Neither gives the required measurement of force.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 732, 734–736.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA

q: A 78-year-old man with multiple sclerosis has erectile dysfunction during exacerbations, improvement during remission, and recurrence with the next exacerbation. Which mechanism best matches the pattern described in Hazzard?
o: Erectile dysfunction associated with vascular disease
Erectile dysfunction associated with medication effects
Erectile dysfunction associated with neurologic disease
Erectile dysfunction associated with psychological distress
explanation:
Erection requires intact neural signaling to the penile vessels and smooth muscle. **Dysfunction that recurs with multiple sclerosis relapses and improves in remission points to a neurologic cause.**

**A. Vascular disease** — Atherosclerosis can limit inflow, but fixed arterial disease is a poor explanation for recovery between neurologic attacks.
**B. Medication effect** — Consider drugs when symptoms track a new prescription or dose change. The changes described here track the disease course.
**C. Neurologic disease** — Multiple sclerosis can disrupt pathways involved in erection. Their fluctuating function accounts for the pattern across successive attacks.
**D. Psychological distress** — Anxiety can impair erections, but the case gives a closer temporal association with neurologic relapses.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 550–551.
ref: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.550–551
chapterTitle: Sexuality, Sexual Function, and the Aging Man
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.550–551

q: A hospital uses a Mobile Acute Care of the Elderly (MACE) team for older medical and surgical inpatients. Which description matches this service?
o: A dedicated rehabilitation ward providing prolonged inpatient recovery
An interdisciplinary ward team reducing the hazards of hospitalization
A home-visiting team providing acute care instead of hospitalization
A scheduled day-clinic team providing outpatient geriatric assessment
explanation:
Mobile Acute Care of the Elderly (MACE) brings geriatric care to older patients on their existing medical or surgical wards. The team works with ward staff to reduce hazards such as immobility, educate families, and prepare for discharge.

**A. Dedicated rehabilitation ward.** Transfer to a rehabilitation unit serves patients who need ongoing recovery after an acute illness.
**B. Interdisciplinary ward team.** A geriatrician, clinical nurse specialists, and social workers can address risks at the bedside while the patient stays on the admitting ward.
**C. Acute care at home.** Hospital-at-home teams deliver acute treatment in the patient's residence.
**D. Day clinic.** Scheduled geriatric assessments serve outpatients and take place outside the inpatient ward.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 194.
ref: Hazzard Ch 14 — MODELS OF HOSPITAL AND OUTPATIENT CARE
chapterTitle: Models of Hospital and Outpatient Care

q: אישה עם דמנציה בינונית וקושי בבליעה לא הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. מבקשים להחיל עליה את המלצות הוועדה הארצית על PEG בחולה עם קיהיון הנוטה למות. כיצד מתייחס המסמך לקבוצה זו?
o: הוא ממליץ בה על PEG לפי עצם קיומה של דמנציה
הוא משאיר את ההחלטה לגבי קבוצה זו פתוחה
הוא ממליץ בה להפסיק בירור בליעה לפני האכלה
הוא ממליץ בה להימנע מצינור לפי ציון קוגניטיבי
explanation:
המלצות המותב עוסקות בהזנת אדם עם קיהיון שנקבע כי הוא נוטה למות. דמנציה בינונית עם דיספגיה אינה כשלעצמה קביעה כזו. **הוא משאיר את ההחלטה לגבי קבוצה זו פתוחה**.

**א. הוא ממליץ בה על PEG לפי עצם קיומה של דמנציה.** אין הוראה להתקין צינור לכל אדם עם דמנציה.
**ב. הוא משאיר את ההחלטה לגבי קבוצה זו פתוחה.** לגבי חולים שאינם בתחום המוגדר אין הכרעה גורפת במסמך.
**ג. הוא ממליץ בה להפסיק בירור בליעה לפני האכלה.** עדיין נדרשת הערכת בליעה ותזונה.
**ד. הוא ממליץ בה להימנע מצינור לפי ציון קוגניטיבי.** ציון קוגניטיבי אינו קובע לבדו את דרך ההזנה.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות, עמ׳ 1.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות

q: A 79-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and a recent ischemic stroke undergoes comprehensive geriatric assessment on a stroke ward. She has residual left hemiparesis and mild dysphasia. Before the stroke she was independent and managed complex finances for her small business. Medications include apixaban 5 mg twice daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Creatinine clearance is 48 mL/min. During a review of venous thromboembolism prevention, which statement about prevention methods agrees with Hazzard?
o: Mechanical devices generally prevent VTE more effectively than pharmacologic agents.
Apixaban is among the approved pharmacologic regimens for VTE prevention.
High bleeding risk generally favors pharmacologic agents over mechanical devices.
High VTE risk favors pharmacologic prophylaxis before estimating bleeding risk.
explanation:
VTE prevention requires balancing thrombosis and bleeding while recognizing anticoagulation already in use. **Apixaban is specifically approved for DVT prophylaxis after elective hip or knee replacement.** That approval is not a recommendation to add prophylactic apixaban on an acute stroke ward.

**A. Mechanical devices are generally more effective.** Pharmacologic prophylaxis often affords greater protection when safe, while mechanical methods have an important role when bleeding risk is high.
**B. Approved apixaban prophylaxis.** Orthopedic replacement is the specific indication. This patient already receives therapeutic apixaban for AF. Verify the poststroke anticoagulation plan and do not add duplicate anticoagulation.
**C. High bleeding risk favors drugs.** Mechanical measures are often preferred when drug prophylaxis is unsafe.
**D. Treat high clot risk before assessing bleeding.** Consider both risks, particularly after a recent cerebral infarct.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1522. FDA Eliquis prescribing information, prophylaxis following hip or knee replacement surgery.
ref: Hazzard Ch 96 — COAGULATION DISORDERS

q: An 86-year-old man with moderate dementia, heart failure (EF 40%), and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24; Cockcroft-Gault CrCl 22 mL/min) physically resists care and has thrown a cup at another resident. He takes donepezil 10 mg, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and furosemide 20 mg daily. After assessing contributors and trying nonpharmacologic measures, dangerous aggression persists. If the risk-benefit assessment favors risperidone, which prescribing approach matches Hazzard?
o: Start low, monitor adverse effects, and titrate to the effective dose
Start at a high dose, then reduce treatment when behavioral control is established
Start several psychotropic drugs together, then identify the most useful combination
Continue treatment without a stop plan, using sedation as the principal target
explanation:
Risperidone may be considered for persistent dangerous aggression in dementia after reversible causes and behavioral measures are addressed. **Start low, monitor harms and titrate to the minimum effective dose**, particularly with CKD and heart disease.

**A. Start low.** Track target aggression alongside orthostasis, sedation and movement effects.
**B. Start high.** A large initial exposure increases adverse effects before individual sensitivity is known.
**C. Several new drugs.** Simultaneous changes make benefit and toxicity difficult to attribute.
**D. Sedation without a stop plan.** The goal is safe behavior with preserved function and regular review of need.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 927.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: A patient with Parkinson disease develops motor worsening after starting metoclopramide. Which mechanism-and-risk pairing explains the Beers recommendation to avoid it?
o: Dopamine-receptor blockade with a risk of worsening parkinsonian symptoms
Dopamine-receptor activation with a risk of worsening parkinsonian symptoms
Dopamine-receptor blockade with an expected improvement in parkinsonian symptoms
Dopamine-receptor activation with an expected improvement in parkinsonian symptoms
explanation:
Metoclopramide relieves nausea partly through dopamine D2 receptor blockade. Blockade in motor pathways can aggravate the movement disorder already present in Parkinson disease.

**Dopamine-receptor blockade can worsen parkinsonian symptoms.** New rigidity or slowing after starting this antiemetic is a reason to review its use.

**A. Blockade with worsening.** Antagonism reduces dopamine signaling in the basal ganglia and can worsen movement.
**B. Activation with worsening.** Metoclopramide is a receptor antagonist. It does not stimulate dopamine receptors.
**C. Blockade with improvement.** Parkinsonian slowness and rigidity can worsen when central dopamine signaling is blocked.
**D. Activation with improvement.** This pairing describes the intended motor effect of a dopamine agonist, a different drug class.

Reference · American Geriatrics Society 2023 Beers Criteria, Table 3, p. 2067.
ref: AGS Beers Criteria 2023 — pp 2067

q: גבר בישראל עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה מבקש לערוך ייפוי כוח מתמשך. מהו העיקרון שעל פיו יש לבחון את יכולתו ואת בחירתו, לפי מדריך משרד המשפטים?
o: לבחון את אבחנתו הקוגניטיבית כמדד מכריע ליכולת עריכת המסמך
לבחון את הסכמת המשפחה כמדד מכריע לרצון לעריכת המסמך
לבחון הבנת העניין ויכולת החלטה לצד בחירה מרצון חופשי
לבחון את עצמאותו בניהול כספים כמדד מכריע להבנת המסמך
explanation:
עריכת ייפוי כוח מתמשך דורשת הבנה של המינוי, מטרותיו ותוצאותיו ובחירה ללא כפייה. **לבחון הבנת העניין ויכולת החלטה לצד בחירה מרצון חופשי**.

**א. לבחון את אבחנתו הקוגניטיבית כמדד מכריע ליכולת עריכת המסמך.** האבחנה מעוררת שאלה לבדיקה אך אינה מכריעה.
**ב. לבחון את הסכמת המשפחה כמדד מכריע לרצון לעריכת המסמך.** המשפחה אינה נותנת הסכמה במקום הממנה.
**ג. לבחון הבנת העניין ויכולת החלטה לצד בחירה מרצון חופשי.** הבדיקה מתייחסת לעניין המסוים ולרצון החופשי.
**ד. לבחון את עצמאותו בניהול כספים כמדד מכריע להבנת המסמך.** קושי בניהול כספים אינו מבחן יחיד להבנה של מינוי רפואי.

אסמכתא · משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך, עמ׳ 4.
ref: משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך

q: An 84-year-old woman with advanced lung disease says that she wants her life to end. How should questions about suicide be approached according to Hazzard?
o: Delay direct questioning because it increases suicidal ideation
Infer suicidal intent from the severity of physical symptoms
Ask directly about thoughts and intent, then about a plan
Infer suicidal intent from the views expressed by her family
explanation:
A wish for life to end can reflect suffering, passive thoughts or active suicidal intent. **Ask directly about thoughts, intent and any plan** to distinguish these possibilities and guide immediate care.

**A. Delay direct questioning.** Asking about suicide does not itself induce suicidal ideation.
**B. Infer intent from lung disease.** Physical suffering alone cannot show whether she plans to act.
**C. Ask directly.** Her account, current safety, risk factors and supports guide the response.
**D. Infer intent from family.** Collateral information helps but cannot replace speaking with her.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1030.
ref: Hazzard Ch 66 — GENERAL TOPICS IN GERIATRIC PSYCHIATRY

q: A 78-year-old man with mild Alzheimer dementia and diabetes has become more confused over two days. He lives with his wife, who manages his medications. Serum sodium is 122 mEq/L. She recently gave him additional 'water tablets' for swollen ankles. Which medication-history focus is specifically supported by Hazzard's discussion of hyponatremia?
o: Clarify thiazide exposure as a cause of falsely low sodium without a water-balance disturbance
Clarify thiazide exposure as a cause of high sodium from impaired water retention
Clarify thiazide exposure as a recognized medication-related contributor to low sodium
Clarify thiazide exposure as evidence favoring gastrointestinal rather than medication-related sodium loss
explanation:
Thiazide diuretics are important causes of true hyponatremia in older adults. **Identify the exact water tablet, dose and timing of the additional doses** while assessing his confusion and sodium of 122.

**A. Falsely low sodium.** Thiazides can cause a real disturbance of renal sodium and water handling.
**B. High sodium.** The drug-related electrolyte pattern under consideration is low sodium.
**C. Thiazide-associated low sodium.** Recent extra doses make medication reconciliation particularly important. Assess other contributors as well.
**D. Gastrointestinal loss.** There is no reported gastrointestinal loss. The history points directly to possible excess diuretic exposure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 586–587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: מטופל הסובל מדמנציה עם קושי ניכר בתפקוד השפתי. המטופל מסוגל להבין משפטים פשוטים, אך לא משפטים מורכבים. קיימת אפרקסיה שפתית. מה סביר למצוא מבחינה פתולוגית?
o: פתולוגיה מסוג TAU
פתולוגיה TDP-43
פגיעה וסקולרית מפושטת
משקעי חלבון 14-3-3
explanation:
Nonfluent or agrammatic primary progressive aphasia impairs speech production and comprehension of complex grammar. **Tau pathology is a common correlate of speech apraxia with preserved simple comprehension**.

**A. Tau.** Frontotemporal tauopathies are often associated with this language phenotype.
**B. TDP-43.** This is more characteristic of semantic PPA, where single-word meaning deteriorates.
**C. Diffuse vascular injury.** A vascular lesion explaining the deficit would argue against primary progressive aphasia.
**D. 14-3-3.** CSF 14-3-3 can mark rapid neuronal injury in suspected prion disease. A protein deposit of this type is not characteristic of agrammatic PPA.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 873, 876.
Key note: Both tau and 14-3-3 received credit. Hazzard associates agrammatic PPA with tau and discusses 14-3-3 in the evaluation of rapidly progressive prion disease.
ref: Hazzard 8e · p. 873-875

q: מה מאפיין את תוחלת החיים בישראל על פי לקט הנתונים של מכון ברוקדייל?
o: תוחלת החיים של גברים יציבה ב- 40 השנים האחרונות.
תוחלת החיים בנשים גבוהה ב-4 שנים מגברים
ישראל היא השנייה בעולם בתוחלת החיים אחרי יפן
תוחלת החיים של נשים עלתה ב-10 שנים מאז 1995
explanation:
**תוחלת החיים בלידה בישראל הייתה גבוהה בנשים בכארבע שנים.** בנתוני 2022 היו הערכים 84.8 שנים לנשים ו־80.7 לגברים, פער של 4.1 שנים.

**א. יציבות בגברים במשך ארבעה עשורים.** תוחלת החיים בגברים עלתה לאורך התקופה.
**ב. פער של כארבע שנים.** ההשוואה מתייחסת לתוחלת חיים בלידה, לא ליתרת החיים בגיל 65.
**ג. מקום שני בעולם.** זהו דירוג אחר התלוי בשנה ובאוכלוסיות ההשוואה.
**ד. עלייה של עשר שנים מאז 1995.** העלייה המדווחת בנשים קטנה מן הערך המוצע.

אסמכתא · מכון ברוקדייל, בני 65+ בישראל, שנתון 2024, עמ׳ 35, 131 ולוח 2.1.
ref: לקט נתונים אינפוגרפי
referenceNote: Brookdale yearbook: לקט נתונים אינפוגרפי. Examined on an earlier edition; figures may differ from the required 2024 edition.

q:
בן 83, מתגורר במחלקה סיעודית. ברקע סובל מ-COPD, יתר לחץ דם, דמנציה מסוג אלצהיימר בדרגת חומרה קלה ושבריריות בולטת. המטופל נוטל את התרופות הבאות:  
 AMLODIPINE 10 mg x 1  
 FUROSEMIDE 40 mg x 1  
 RISPERDONE 1 mg X2  
 DOPICAR 1 tab x 3  
 ASPIRIN 100 mg x1  
 DONEPAZIL 10 mg x1  
 FESOTERODINE 8 mg x1  
 משאפים לטיפול כרוני ב-COPD. בבדיקה- לחץ דם 150/80, דופק סדיר 82, בצקת פריפרית בקרסוליים אבל ללא סימנים נוספים לאי-ספיקת לב. בבדיקה נוירולוגית- ברדיקינזיה וריגידיות. כל הבאים הם קסקדה טיפולית פרט לאחד. איזה שילוב תרופות לא מהווה קסקדה טיפולית?
o: RISPERDONE ו- DOPICAR
DONEPEZIL ו- TOVIAZ
AMLODIPINE ו- FUSID
DOPICAR ו- FUSID
explanation:
A prescribing cascade links two drugs through a particular adverse effect of the first. This resident has ankle edema and parkinsonism, and his medication list also suggests a possible bladder-treatment cascade.

**Dopicar and Fusid are the exception.** Levodopa/carbidopa can be the response to antipsychotic-induced parkinsonism, and furosemide can be the response to amlodipine-related edema. They occupy the treatment ends of different cascades.

**A. Risperidone and Dopicar.** Risperidone can cause rigidity and bradykinesia. Adding levodopa/carbidopa for those signs can treat a drug effect as new Parkinson disease.
**B. Donepezil and Toviaz.** Donepezil can cause urgency or incontinence, prompting fesoterodine, a bladder antimuscarinic.
**C. Amlodipine and Fusid.** Amlodipine can cause ankle edema even without heart failure. Treating that edema with furosemide is a typical cascade.
**D. Dopicar and Fusid.** This pairing has no corresponding adverse-effect link in the case. The competing explanations for the diuretic and Parkinson treatment are different.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 304–306, Table 22-2.
ref: Hazzard 8e · p. 305 · Table 22-2

q: An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with an acute illness is being considered for an Acute Care for Elders (ACE) unit. Which outcome pattern matches the randomized trials described in Hazzard?
o: Less disability at discharge and a shorter hospital stay.
More disability at discharge and a shorter hospital stay.
Less disability at discharge and more transitions to skilled nursing care.
More disability at discharge and fewer transitions to skilled nursing care.
explanation:
An Acute Care for Elders unit integrates mobility, function-focused nursing and discharge planning during hospitalization. Trial outcomes included **less disability at discharge and a shorter stay**.

**A. Less disability at discharge and a shorter hospital stay.** Preserving function and organizing care early can improve both outcomes.
**B. More disability at discharge and a shorter hospital stay.** A shorter stay is consistent with the trials, but greater disability reverses the functional finding.
**C. Less disability at discharge and more transitions to skilled nursing care.** Less disability is correct, but more skilled-nursing transitions is the wrong direction.
**D. More disability at discharge and fewer transitions to skilled nursing care.** The claim of greater disability reverses the observed functional benefit.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 194.
ref: Hazzard Ch 14 — MODELS OF HOSPITAL AND OUTPATIENT CARE

q: What is the single most important, validated risk factor for Alzheimer disease?
o: Low educational attainment
Traumatic brain injury
Advancing chronological age
Habitual physical inactivity
explanation:
A risk factor can be strongly predictive without being modifiable. Both the incidence and the proportion of people living with Alzheimer disease rise sharply across successive older age groups.

**Advancing chronological age** has the strongest established association with Alzheimer risk across older adults.

**A. Less education.** Limited schooling is associated with higher risk, possibly through differences in cognitive reserve, but age has the stronger overall association.
**B. Traumatic brain injury.** A history of head injury can raise susceptibility, especially with severe or repeated injury. It is not the dominant predictor across older adults.
**C. Advancing age.** The steep age gradient applies across a broad range of backgrounds and exposures.
**D. Physical inactivity.** Inactivity is a modifiable midlife risk, useful for prevention counseling, but less important than age as an overall predictor.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 894, 896–897.
ref: Hazzard 8e Ch 59 · p894

q: What does the Frailty Index express in the deficit-accumulation approach described by Hazzard?
o: The proportion of considered deficits that are present in the person
The absolute deficit count without reference to the number considered
The identity of a fixed deficit combination rather than its proportion
The weighted severity of deficits rather than an unweighted deficit count
explanation:
The deficit-accumulation model summarizes the burden of abnormalities across several systems. **Its index is the proportion of considered deficits present in the individual.**

**A. Proportion of deficits present** — Dividing by the total considered makes the result interpretable even when valid versions contain different numbers of items.
**B. Absolute number alone** — Ten deficits among twenty assessed and ten among fifty yield different proportions and different FI values.
**C. One fixed combination** — No particular combination of deficits is required. Many different profiles can give the same fraction.
**D. Severity-weighted deficits** — The model described here uses an unweighted count. It does not assign larger causal or prognostic weights to selected diagnoses.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 623, Frailty as a Deficit Accumulation.
ref: Hazzard 8e Ch 42 · p623

q: Why might delaying surgery for optimization be harmful?
o: Emergency surgery may lower mortality compared with elective surgery
Anesthesia type may determine outcomes after baseline risk is controlled
Operator experience may predict 7-day mortality better than preoperative risk factors
A needed elective procedure may become a higher-risk emergency while waiting
explanation:
Preoperative optimization is intended to reduce an identifiable, modifiable risk. **Delay itself can cause harm if a needed elective procedure becomes an emergency.**

**A. Emergency surgery lowers mortality** Older adults undergoing emergency surgery experience particularly high complication and mortality rates.
**B. Anesthetic type determines the result** In the comparison described, spinal versus general anesthesia did not predict outcome after adjustment for baseline risk.
**C. Operator experience best predicts seven-day mortality** Preoperative risk factors predicted early mortality better than anesthesiologist experience or anesthesia duration.
**D. Progression while waiting** Consider the natural history of the surgical disease and the likely benefit of extra preparation before postponing an intervention.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 27, p. 376, Emergency Surgeries and Period of Risk.
ref: Hazzard 8e Ch 27 · p376

explanation:
In symptomatic HFrEF, iron deficiency can worsen exercise capacity independently of congestion. Microcytosis, high transferrin and ferritin of 30 ng/mL support **IV iron replacement** while evaluating the cause of iron loss.

**A. Oral iron.** Oral supplementation has not shown the same functional benefit in iron-deficient heart failure trials.
